grade.reason: The agent's change to mitmproxy/net/tls.py is functionally identical to the merged patch. It moves set_min_proto_version, set_max_proto_version and the SSL.Connection setup inside the existing try block, ahead of recv(). A setup-time SSL.Error is therefore caught by the existing except SSL.Error handler and the function returns False. The agent also added the regression test. The merged patch's CHANGELOG entry does not affect behavior.

result:
`is_supported_version()` in `mitmproxy/net/tls.py` now reports a version as unsupported (`return False`) when OpenSSL rejects it at setup time, instead of raising. I haven't run the tests, per your instructions.

The two `set_min/max_proto_version` calls and the `SSL.Connection` setup now sit inside the existing `try`, ahead of the `recv()` probe. That way an `SSL.Error` from an OpenSSL build that has dropped a protocol version (such as SSLv3) is handled the same way as one from the probe. Versions that are currently supported behave as before.

I added `test_supported_setup_error` to `test/mitmproxy/net/test_tls.py`. It monkeypatches `SSL.Context.set_min_proto_version` to raise `SSL.Error` and asserts that `is_supported_version(Version.SSL3)` returns falsy. This reproduces the crash on any OpenSSL build.
